articles.title: LIC Plan Comparison Tool: FastAPI & React Workflow
articles.excerpt: Problem LIC agents in India often juggle dozens of plans while presenting them to clients. The traditional approach—static PDFs or spreadsheets—leads to duplicated effort, stale bonus data, and slow p…
articles.body: Problem LIC agents in India often juggle dozens of plans while presenting them to clients. The traditional approach—static PDFs or spreadsheets—leads to duplicated effort, stale bonus data, and slow page loads when a new plan is added. A digital tool that loads only the necessary code for a chosen plan, while isolating runtime errors, directly addresses these pain points. Implementation Overview The DoAide InsureKit achieves this with a combination of FastAPI on the back‑end, React + Vite on the front‑end, and a PostgreSQL database that stores plan metadata and current bonus rates. The most visible technical improvement is route‑level code splitting coupled with an error boundary . Route‑Level Code Splitting Vite, the bundler used in this project, supports dynamic imports out of the box.
articles.author: Subhendu Das

articles.title: Send Contracts via WhatsApp with DoAide Contract Generator
articles.excerpt: Problem Indian SMB owners, freelancers, and startups often need to share newly generated contracts—NDAs, employment contracts, service agreements—quickly with clients or partners. Sending a PDF by ema…
articles.body: Problem Indian SMB owners, freelancers, and startups often need to share newly generated contracts—NDAs, employment contracts, service agreements—quickly with clients or partners. Sending a PDF by email or uploading it to a cloud folder adds friction and delays the signing process. This is where contract generator pays off in practice. How the Feature Works DoAide Contracts adds a single‑click WhatsApp share button after a contract is generated. The flow is: Generate : The user selects a template (e.g., employment contract template ) and fills in the form. Store : FastAPI saves the contract as a PDF blob in PostgreSQL and returns a contract ID. Share : The React UI renders a Share via WhatsApp button.

articles.title: Before You Click Swap on AviorSwap: The Details Worth Checking
articles.excerpt: Crypto interfaces have become more accessible, but I think one habit remains important regardless of how simple a platform looks: understanding a transaction before confirming it. A swap may take only…
articles.body: Crypto interfaces have become more accessible, but I think one habit remains important regardless of how simple a platform looks: understanding a transaction before confirming it. A swap may take only a few clicks, yet several details can affect the result. That's one reason I find the user experience of exchange platforms such as AviorSwap worth discussing. The amount you send is only half the picture When exchanging tokens, it's natural to focus on the amount being sold. But the estimated amount received deserves just as much attention. The final result can depend on the available liquidity, the exchange route, network conditions, and applicable fees. A useful interface should make the expected output visible before confirmation.

articles.title: Keeping Vector Retrieval Stable While Your Knowledge Base Is Still Loading
articles.excerpt: Keeping Vector Retrieval Stable While Your Knowledge Base Is Still Loading At 3:17 AM, your agent platform stops responding. Ingestion workers are retrying document chunks. Retrieval latency has spike…
articles.body: Keeping Vector Retrieval Stable While Your Knowledge Base Is Still Loading At 3:17 AM, your agent platform stops responding. Ingestion workers are retrying document chunks. Retrieval latency has spiked from 80ms to 4 seconds. The HNSW index is fine. The problem is that ingestion and retrieval are fighting over the same PostgreSQL pages, and neither path has backpressure logic. This is the production failure that tutorials skip. I am evaluating Tencent/WeKnora as an external integrator, using its stated document-to-RAG, agent, and self-maintaining Wiki scope. The design below is a proposed PostgreSQL retrieval boundary, not a claim about WeKnora's current implementation or measured performance.

articles.title: Why I built my coding-agent tooling as a local proxy instead of hooks
articles.excerpt: There are dozens of coding agents out there now, with a new one every other week. Using them extensively, both at work and on side projects, I kept having ideas about the requests they send, how I cou…
articles.body: There are dozens of coding agents out there now, with a new one every other week. Using them extensively, both at work and on side projects, I kept having ideas about the requests they send, how I could optimize them, or build around them to improve my workflows: What if a small local model checked them for secrets first? What if I could see where my tokens actually go? What if old tool output could be trimmed before it's sent again? The sensible move was to pick one tool like Claude Code or Codex CLI, build on that tool's hooks, and call it a day. In true side project fashion, that's not what happened. Where to put it Every coding agent has its own extension point: hooks, config, plugins.

articles.title: Australia's bizarre 'Spider Crater' seen from orbit | Space photo of the day for Oct. 22, 2026
articles.excerpt: A satellite image of "Spider Crater" in Western Australia.
articles.body: A satellite image of "Spider Crater" in Western Australia. (Image credit: NASA Earth Observatory image by Michala Garrison, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey ) From the dangerous Sydney funnel-web to the common huntsman, Australia is home to its fair share of spiders. It even has a crater shaped like one. What is it? One stretch of the vast Western Australia wilderness is imprinted with a curious crater, which likely formed after a meteor impact hundreds of millions of years ago. Geologists think the spider-like pattern in the crater's center was created when its floor rebounded following the initial impact, NASA has said . In the hundreds of millions of years since the initial impact, erosion has continued to carve this formation into its current, signature shape.

articles.body: The writing was on the wall, but the news still hit us like a truck yesterday. BioWare, the iconic RPG studio behind the Mass Effect and Dragon Age series, is no more. Development on the next Mass Effect has stopped, but EA might not be entirely done with the IP. Variety reported, backed by EA’s own statement and BioWare’s goodbye on socials , that EA is laying off 3% of its global workforce and closing down BioWare. The shift comes shortly after the company went fully private this summer , with Saudi Arabia and private equity acquiring it alongside all its studios and properties.

articles.body: NASA will provide an update about its Artemis moon plans on Friday (Oct. 23), and you can watch it live. The news will come during a press conference at the agency's Kennedy Space Center in Florida, which starts Friday at 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT). You can watch it live here at Space.com, courtesy of NASA. articles.title: Faster to Science: A Letter to the Science Community
articles.excerpt: NASA Science wants to deliver science faster, so we’re changing how we compete and select missions. On Monday, October 26, we will host a virtual NASA Science Town Hall.
articles.body: Dear NASA Science Community, NASA Science wants to deliver science faster, so we’re changing how we compete and select missions. On Monday, October 26, we will host a virtual NASA Science Town Hall, from NASA Headquarters, to explain our new Competition Model 2.0 (CM 2.0), and answer your questions. ( Details below. ) We have heard you. We have listened. We know that the burden of bringing great ideas forward has been too heavy for too long. It has taken years to move mission concepts through the current two-step process. This has often come with contract management challenges, unpredictability, and not enough funding. NASA is committed to doing better — and I’m excited to share with you how we’re making it happen.
